title: Salted Caramel Chocolate Tart with Pecans
changes_from_base: A press-in cocoa-almond crust, a layer of homemade salted caramel with pecans, and an unbaked ganache top instead of baked custard.
summary: A cocoa-almond press-in crust with a layer of homemade salted caramel and pecans, under a smooth dark ganache.
equipment: mixing bowl and wooden spoon (or stand mixer)

ingredients.item: soft unsalted butter, plus extra for greasing
fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt

ingredients.note: check the label for milk and soya

steps.title: Crust dough
steps.text: grease the tin. Beat the butter, sugar, salt and espresso powder until smooth, then mix in the flour, ground almonds, cocoa and water until it comes together.

steps.title: Press and chill
steps.text: press the dough evenly over the base and sides of the tin, prick all over with the fork and freeze 15-20 min. Heat the oven to 200 °C (180 °C fan).

steps.title: Bake the crust
steps.text: bake on the tray for 15-18 min, until set and smelling of chocolate, then cool.

steps.title: Caramel
steps.text: heat the sugar and 60 ml water in the pan, swirling, until it dissolves, then boil without stirring to a deep amber. Off the heat, whisk in the warm cream carefully, as it will spit, then the butter and salt. Simmer, whisking, until it reaches 108 °C, then cool 10 min. Use a long whisk and stand back when the cream goes in.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: scatter half the pecans in the crust, pour the caramel over and freeze 30 min, until firm.

steps.title: Chocolate
steps.text: heat the 140 ml cream until steaming, pour it over the chocolate, leave 5 min and stir smooth. Pour over the cold caramel and scatter the rest of the pecans on top.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: refrigerate at least 1 h. Take it out 15-20 min before serving and sprinkle with the flaky salt. It cuts best slightly cool, not straight from the fridge.

tips: Take the caramel to a deep amber colour for the best flavour, but not smoking.
Warm the cream first so the caramel does not seize.
Toast the pecans in a dry pan until fragrant before chopping.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 5 days, or freeze for up to 2 months.
